findings.body: Every instance carries the same timestamp — the moment the module was first imported — instead of the time the assignment was queued, so `queued` (and the value in `to_dict()`/task payloads) is stale and useless for debouncing or latency logging.
findings.failure_mode: Silently incorrect data: timestamps never advance for the lifetime of the process.
findings.impact: Every instance carries the same timestamp — the moment the module was first imported — instead of the time the assignment was queued, so `queued` (and the value in `to_dict()`/task payloads) is stale and useless for debouncing or latency logging.
findings.root_cause: A dataclass field default was given a called value (`timezone.now()`) instead of a `default_factory`, so it is bound once at class-creation time.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `queued: datetime = field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so the default is computed per instance.
findings.title: `queued` default evaluated once at import time
findings.trigger: Any `AssignmentSource(...)` or `AssignmentSource.from_integration(...)` construction after the module is imported (e.g. an inbound Jira webhook assigning a group).
findings.verifier_reason: Line 18 shows `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` as a dataclass field default. This is evaluated once at class definition time, not per-instance. All instances will share the same timestamp from module import. This is a well-known Python dataclass pitfall.

pr.body:
## The problem:
When a Jira issue's `assignee` field is quickly modified multiple times in a row, we end up assigning and resyncing the assignees to Jira, which causes a loop. This is because _all_ inbound integration webhooks that modify an issue assignment generate an outbound update for all issue sync integrations as well.

## Solution:
This PR adds a new `AssignmentSource` dataclass, which acts as a context carrier when an external webhook triggers an issue assignment change. This is then checked on the outbound sync logic, preventing the change from being propagated to the same integration that initially triggered the change.
pr.title: fix(ecosystem): Breaks issue sync cycles

raw_findings.body: Every instance carries the same timestamp — the moment the module was first imported — instead of the time the assignment was queued, so `queued` (and the value in `to_dict()`/task payloads) is stale and useless for debouncing or latency logging.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Silently incorrect data: timestamps never advance for the lifetime of the process.
raw_findings.impact: Every instance carries the same timestamp — the moment the module was first imported — instead of the time the assignment was queued, so `queued` (and the value in `to_dict()`/task payloads) is stale and useless for debouncing or latency logging.
raw_findings.root_cause: A dataclass field default was given a called value (`timezone.now()`) instead of a `default_factory`, so it is bound once at class-creation time.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use `queued: datetime = field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so the default is computed per instance.
raw_findings.title: `queued` default evaluated once at import time
raw_findings.trigger: Any `AssignmentSource(...)` or `AssignmentSource.from_integration(...)` construction after the module is imported (e.g. an inbound Jira webhook assigning a group).

raw_findings.body: The datetime must survive the broker serializer: with a JSON task serializer the enqueue raises an encode error (outbound assignee sync silently stops), and where the serializer stringifies datetimes the worker rebuilds `AssignmentSource` with `queued` typed as `str`, violating the declared `datetime` annotation because `from_dict` performs no type validation.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Task enqueue error or silent type drift of a cross-process payload field.
raw_findings.impact: The datetime must survive the broker serializer: with a JSON task serializer the enqueue raises an encode error (outbound assignee sync silently stops), and where the serializer stringifies datetimes the worker rebuilds `AssignmentSource` with `queued` typed as `str`, violating the declared `datetime` annotation because `from_dict` performs no type validation.
raw_findings.root_cause: `to_dict()` returns the raw dataclass `asdict()` output, including a non-primitive `datetime`, and it is used as a celery task argument without an explicit serialization contract.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Serialize `queued` explicitly (e.g. `queued.isoformat()` in `to_dict()` and parse it back in `from_dict()`), or omit `queued` from the task payload entirely.
raw_findings.title: Datetime is placed directly into celery task kwargs
raw_findings.trigger: An inbound integration webhook assigns/deassigns a group, so `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async` is called with `assignment_source_dict` containing the `queued` `datetime` produced by `asdict()`.

raw_findings.body: The declared parameter is dead — `sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_status_outbound.py` never passes it, so status sync cycles are still unprotected — and calling with the documented keyword raises `TypeError: sync_status_outbound() got an unexpected keyword argument 'assignment_source'` for implementations that do not accept `**kwargs`.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Interface contract diverges from implementations; the intended cycle protection for status sync is not actually wired up.
raw_findings.impact: The declared parameter is dead — `sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_status_outbound.py` never passes it, so status sync cycles are still unprotected — and calling with the documented keyword raises `TypeError: sync_status_outbound() got an unexpected keyword argument 'assignment_source'` for implementations that do not accept `**kwargs`.
raw_findings.root_cause: The abstract base signature was widened without updating the single call site or the concrete subclass overrides, creating an unimplementable/unused contract.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Either drop `assignment_source` from the abstract signature in this PR, or thread it through the `sync_status_outbound` task/`should_sync("outbound_status", ...)` call and add the parameter to all concrete overrides (example, jira, jira_server, vsts).
raw_findings.title: `assignment_source` added to abstract `sync_status_outbound` but never threaded or implemented

raw_findings.body: The actual regression this PR fixes (webhook-driven inbound assignment re-syncing outbound to the same integration) is unverified; a future refactor that drops `assignment_source` from these `assign`/`deassign` calls would pass CI while reintroducing the sync loop.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Regression in the fixed behavior can be reintroduced without any test failure.
raw_findings.impact: The actual regression this PR fixes (webhook-driven inbound assignment re-syncing outbound to the same integration) is unverified; a future refactor that drops `assignment_source` from these `assign`/`deassign` calls would pass CI while reintroducing the sync loop.
raw_findings.root_cause: New behavior was added at the inbound sync call sites while tests only exercise `GroupAssignee.objects.assign` with a manually constructed `AssignmentSource`.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a test in `tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py` (or a sync util test) that invokes `sync_group_assignee_inbound(integration, email, key)` with an `ExampleIntegration` link and asserts `ExampleIntegration.sync_assignee_outbound` is not called for that same integration.
